newsitem.title: USA: FAA to weigh comments on St. Louis airport plan.
newsitem.headline: FAA to weigh comments on St. Louis airport plan.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration will sort through about 15,000 public comments on plans to expand Lambert-St. Louis International Airport, an FAA official said Friday.

Mike Faltermeier, manager of planning and programming for the FAA's airports division's central region, said that public response was "very good" during the comment period that ended Friday. He said the FAA would now evaluate the comments before issuing a final environmental impact statement for the project.
"We were not surprised by the number of comments at an airport like St. Louis," he said.

In September, the FAA issued a draft statement that St. Louis officials said favored a so-called W-1W plan. The $1.88 billion plan calls for a new 9,000-foot-long parallel runway that would allow for airline operations during inclement weather, as well as terminal and road improvements.

Faltermeier said the scope of the public comments would determine when the FAA would complete the final environmental report. He added that the agency's record of decision would probably follow the release of that report by 30 days.
St. Louis officials have said the expansion plan would be financed largely with general airport revenue bonds and possibly with bonds backed by passenger facility charges.
